subject: Pivotal Health: multi-year prepay ramp & term discount — exec approval
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@pivotalhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@pivotalhealth.com>; Pivotal Health Legal <legal@pivotalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood prepay — clarification on ramp / term discount

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We’re close to an internal go/no-go but procurement has two asks before we can move forward: 1) flexibility on the first-year ramp (we don’t have steady usage for Q1) and 2) a more aggressive term discount for a 3-year prepay vs. the standard schedule you shared.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Allow a front-loaded discount in year 1 with a smaller committed spend in Q1 and a ramp in months 4–12?
- Offer a steeper effective discount if we commit to a 3-year prepay at signing (we were hoping for ~28% effective vs. the 20% in your memo)

We’ll need this clarified for our CFO and procurement to greenlight the SOW and legal review. Attach: our internal budget cadence (Pivotal_Budget_Q2.pdf).

Best,
Elena
Director of Product Innovation
Pivotal Health

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@pivotalhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@pivotalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood prepay — clarification on ramp / term discount

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the budget cadence doc. Short answer: we can be flexible, but the two items together (non-standard ramp + bigger term discount) touch commercial policy and will need a small exec approval.

Proposed approach:
- Technical: allow an initial low-commit (30% of Year1 monthly baseline for months 1–3) with an automated ramp to the committed baseline by month 6. We’ll add a usage-based true-up at month 12. This protects both sides.
- Commercial: offer a 26% effective discount on a 3-year full prepay if we accept the proposed ramp instead of a straight front-loaded credit. To get to 28% I’ll need an approval note from Finance/GM.

I can get this routed to our commercial leadership today — looping in Lauren and Marcus internally for pricing & approval logistics. If you can share the anticipated total prepay amount (topline $ for 3 years), that will speed paperwork.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Memo_Pivotal_20260402.pdf (pricing sketch)

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pivotal prepay asks — need exec sign-off for deeper term discount

Team — forwarding Pivotal’s request. They want: non-standard ramp (protects their Q1) + a 3-yr prepay target of roughly 28% effective discount. I can offer 26% w/out escalation, but 28% requires an exception.

Quick facts:
- Deal size: customer estimating ~$4.2M ARR equivalent over 3 years (prepay $10.5M total) — they will confirm exact $s but this is the working number.
- Risk: front-loaded low usage months increase unit cost for us; we mitigate with true-up and ramp schedule.
- Benefit: long-term committed revenue and strategic reference in healthcare.

Ask: Can we escalate to Finance/GM (Vivek) for a one-time 28% effective term discount on the 3-year prepay, conditional on the ramp schedule below and a signed SOW by 05/07? I’ve attached a redline of the ramp schedule (Pivotal_Ramp_Schedule_v3.xlsx) and a short pricing memo.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-06T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pivotal prepay asks — need exec sign-off for deeper term discount

Aditya — I reviewed the numbers with Marcus. Context from Finance: 26% is within delegated authority for Sales if deal economics include the standard ramp true-up at 12 months. 28% would reduce margin beyond our target for healthcare vertical unless we secure the following mitigations:
- Firm minimum quarterly true-up starting month 4
- DocuSign clause for irreversible prepay (no refunds)
- Commit to an onboarding and usage plan (CS milestones) tied to milestone credits

If you can get Pivotal to accept those conditions we can support escalating to Vivek for a final sign-off. Marcus will prepare the margin impact note. I’ll draft a short approval request email for Vivek.

-Lauren
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-07T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: margin impact note — Pivotal 3yr prepay

Attached is the quick margin model (summary in doc) — we assume typical utilization curve + the proposed ramp (30% months 1–3, 65% months 4–6, 100% month 7+). At $10.5M prepay, 26% yields mid-20s % gross margin; 28% pushes that to low-teens without milestone protections.

Recommendation: escalate for 28% only if Pivotal signs the milestone-locked onboarding SOW and agrees to quarterly minimums at month 4+. If we get those, I can recommend approval with a carve-out for limited one-time marketing credits (mutual PR).

Attachment: SOW_Pivotal_2026.docx (draft with CS milestones)

-Marcus
Dir., Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai; hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec approval request — Pivotal Health 3yr prepay (28% ask)

Vivek — forwarding for your approval. Ask: approve a one-time 28% effective term discount on a 3-year full prepay from Pivotal Health (~$10.5M total upfront), conditional on the ramp schedule and SOW milestones that force quarterly minimums starting month 4 and a 12-month true-up.

Why: strategic healthcare reference, cross-sell potential, multi-region footprint. Risk: lowers gross margin materially without milestone protection. Marcus attached margin note; Lauren recommends proceed to you if Pivotal accepts the milestone-locked SOW.

Please advise: approve / approve with changes / decline. If approved, I’ll send a short exec approval memo to Pivotal and start DocuSign.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai; lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-19T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — Pivotal Health 3yr prepay (28% ask)

Thanks for the thorough context. I approve the one-time 28% effective term discount on the following conditions:
1) Pivotal signs the milestone-locked SOW with quarterly minimums and a 12-month true-up.
2) Legal approves the irreversible prepay clause (no refunds).
3) We include a co-marketing reference clause and a 6-month operational review (CS + product) after month 6.

I’ll ask Legal to prioritize the irreversible clause and finance to reserve the margin carve-out in the forecast. Aditya — proceed to confirm terms with Elena and request DocuSign. Keep me copied on the final SOW.

-Vivek
GM, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pivotal prepay — exec approval granted (terms & next steps)

Elena / Tom — good news: Vivek has approved a one-time 28% effective term discount on a 3-year full prepay, contingent on the following items we discussed:
- Agreed ramp schedule: 30% months 1–3, 65% months 4–6, 100% month 7+. (See attached ramp spreadsheet.)
- Quarterly minimum true-ups starting month 4 and a 12-month annual true-up (to reconcile usage).
- Signed milestone-locked SOW (CS onboarding milestones) — attached draft SOW.

Attachments: Pivotal_Ramp_Schedule_v3.xlsx; SOW_Pivotal_2026.docx; Redwood_Pricing_Memo_Pivotal_20260419.pdf

Best,
